egress.terms: Inherited from the backing store. Two client options matter: `publicurl=` lets downloads skip the S3 API entirely (bucket policy + plain HTTP GET, hence cacheable/CDN-able), and `signature=anonymous` allows read-only public access with no credentials at all.

tooling: git-annex (Haskell, standalone Linux/macOS builds, ~1.5k stars on the mirror). Config via `git annex initremote type=S3 host=... bucket=... requeststyle=path`. Internet Archive has a documented special mode (`host=s3.us.archive.org`) where git-annex writes x-archive-meta-* headers and records the public URL, so every annexed file is also fetchable from archive.org with no login.
chaining: One special remote per bucket; `fileprefix=` lets many remotes share one bucket. The allowance is per account, so each free S3 account adds one bucket. Because git-annex keys content by hash, the S3 side is a dumb blob store. A client can shard the same dataset across several free stores, and git-annex tracks which copy is where (`git annex whereis`). Chunking (`chunk=1MiB`) avoids per-object size caps on the backing store.
limits_note: Depends on backend. Practical: `partsize=1GiB` needed for multipart; parts under 100 MiB are rejected by S3; `versioning=yes` means git-annex cannot drop content. No delete-resume; interrupted uploads restart. For IA specifically, uploads to the test collection vanish after 30 days and public visibility lags.

reliability_note: Mature and boring — the special remote has existed for over a decade. Failure mode is backend-side (IA's S3 endpoint was unreachable during this session: connect timeout on s3.us.archive.org:443, and archive.org/help/abouts3.txt returned 522 through the proxy), not annex-side.
